grammarFocus: 关系从句；指代；可能性表达；复杂句主干辨认。
title: The Library of Lost Sounds: A Reading Inference Challenge
instructions: 阅读下面这篇关于一个模拟社区项目的文章，然后回答10个问题。文章和题目均为模拟材料，不是官方雅思试题。请仔细阅读，注意关系从句、指代和可能性表达。答案必须基于文章内容。
passage:
When Mira Chen first visited the old radio station on the edge of her town, she expected to find nothing but dust and broken equipment. Instead, she discovered a collection of reel-to-reel tapes that had been forgotten for decades. The station, which had closed in 1985, had once been the voice of the local community. Now, Mira, a retired teacher who had always loved stories, decided to bring those voices back to life.

The project, which she called 'The Library of Lost Sounds', began with a simple idea: digitise the tapes and make them available online. However, the task was far from simple. Many of the tapes were damaged, and the machine that could play them was broken. Mira, whose knowledge of electronics was limited, had to rely on volunteers. A local engineer, who preferred to remain anonymous, fixed the machine in exchange for nothing but a thank-you note. 'I just wanted to hear my grandfather's voice again,' he explained. His grandfather had been a newsreader at the station.

As Mira listened to the tapes, she realised that they contained more than just music and news. There were interviews with farmers, shopkeepers, and children, all of whom had shared their everyday lives. One recording, which lasted nearly an hour, featured a group of women discussing the best way to make dumplings. Another, which was only a few minutes long, captured a young boy reading a poem he had written. These recordings, which had seemed unimportant at the time, now offered a window into a vanished world.

Not everything went smoothly. Some tapes had been stored in damp conditions, and the sound quality was poor. Mira had to decide which recordings were worth saving. She might have given up, but the enthusiasm of the volunteers kept her going. 'We can't save everything,' she admitted, 'but we can save what matters most.' The team, which had grown to include students and pensioners, worked patiently, cleaning each tape and transferring its contents to a computer.

The project also raised questions about privacy. Some people, whose relatives appeared on the tapes, were worried about personal information being made public. Mira, who had not anticipated this problem, organised a meeting to discuss it. After a long debate, the group agreed that recordings would be published only if the families gave permission. This decision, which delayed the project by several months, was seen as essential. 'It's not just about technology,' Mira said. 'It's about respect.'

By the end of the year, the Library of Lost Sounds had uploaded over two hundred recordings. The website, which was designed by a local student, allowed visitors to search by date or by name. Mira was surprised by the response. People from all over the country, many of whom had never visited the town, wrote to thank her. Some said they had heard their own grandparents' voices for the first time. Others simply enjoyed the glimpse of everyday life in a small community.

Mira, who is now planning a second phase, hopes to involve more schools. She believes that the project, which started as a personal hobby, has become a valuable educational resource. 'These tapes remind us that history is not just about famous people,' she says. 'It's about ordinary voices, too.' The Library of Lost Sounds, which might have remained hidden forever, now ensures that those voices will not be forgotten.

questions.prompt: What was the original state of the old radio station when Mira first visited it?
options: It was full of dust and broken equipment.
It was already digitised and online.
It was being used as a school.
It had been rebuilt as a museum.
answers: It was full of dust and broken equipment.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确提到Mira预期发现“nothing but dust and broken equipment”，并且她确实发现了被遗忘的磁带。因此选项A正确。
questions.evidence: she expected to find nothing but dust and broken equipment.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the local engineer fix the machine?
options: He wanted to hear his grandfather's voice again.
He was paid a large sum of money.
He was a close friend of Mira's.
answers: He wanted to hear his grandfather's voice again.
questions.explanation: 第二段中工程师说：“I just wanted to hear my grandfather's voice again.” 他祖父曾是电台的新闻播音员。因此选A。
questions.evidence: 'I just wanted to hear my grandfather's voice again,' he explained.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as content found on the tapes?
options: A group of women discussing dumplings.
A young boy reading a poem.
A speech by a famous politician.
answers: A speech by a famous politician.
questions.explanation: 第三段提到了妇女讨论包饺子、男孩读诗、以及农民和店主的采访，但没有提到著名政治家的演讲。因此D是未提及的内容。
questions.evidence: There were interviews with farmers, shopkeepers, and children... One recording... featured a group of women discussing the best way to make dumplings. Another... captured a young boy reading a poem.

questions.prompt: What problem did the project face regarding privacy?
options: Some people were worried about personal information being made public.
The volunteers refused to sign privacy agreements.
answers: Some people were worried about personal information being made public.
questions.explanation: 第五段指出：“Some people, whose relatives appeared on the tapes, were worried about personal information being made public.” 因此A正确。
questions.evidence: Some people, whose relatives appeared on the tapes, were worried about personal information being made public.

questions.prompt: How was the privacy issue resolved?
options: Recordings would be published only with family permission.
The project was moved to another town.
Mira decided to publish everything without permission.
answers: Recordings would be published only with family permission.
questions.explanation: 第五段提到：“the group agreed that recordings would be published only if the families gave permission.” 因此选A。
questions.evidence: the group agreed that recordings would be published only if the families gave permission.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the website's search function?
options: Visitors could search by date or by name.
It was designed by Mira herself.
It required a password to access.
answers: Visitors could search by date or by name.
questions.explanation: 第六段提到：“The website, which was designed by a local student, allowed visitors to search by date or by name.” 因此A正确。
questions.evidence: The website, which was designed by a local student, allowed visitors to search by date or by name.

questions.prompt: What is Mira planning for the second phase of the project?
questions.explanation: 最后一段说：“Mira, who is now planning a second phase, hopes to involve more schools.” 因此选A。
questions.evidence: Mira, who is now planning a second phase, hopes to involve more schools.

questions.prompt: The passage states that the project was delayed by several months. True, False, or Not Given?
questions.explanation: 第五段明确提到：“This decision, which delayed the project by several months, was seen as essential.” 因此该陈述为真。
questions.evidence: This decision, which delayed the project by several months, was seen as essential.

questions.prompt: Mira had anticipated the privacy problem from the beginning. True, False, or Not Given?
questions.explanation: 第五段说：“Mira, who had not anticipated this problem, organised a meeting to discuss it.” 这表明她并未预料到该问题，因此陈述为假。
questions.evidence: Mira, who had not anticipated this problem, organised a meeting to discuss it.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The engineer preferred to remain ________.
questions.explanation: 第二段提到：“A local engineer, who preferred to remain anonymous, fixed the machine...” 因此填入anonymous。
questions.evidence: A local engineer, who preferred to remain anonymous, fixed the machine

grammar.title: 关系从句、指代与复杂句主干辨认
grammar.explanation: 英语中，关系从句用来提供额外信息，常由who, which, whose等引导。指代要明确，如代词it/they指代前文的名词。复杂句的主干是主句的主语和谓语，忽略从句和修饰成分。可能性表达如might have done表示对过去的推测。
grammar.example: The project, which she called 'The Library of Lost Sounds', began with a simple idea.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
questions.explanation: 先行词the woman指人，在从句中作主语，用who。

questions.prompt: What does 'they' refer to in: 'The tapes were damaged, and they could not be played'?
Which sentence expresses a possibility about the past?
options: She might have forgotten the meeting.
answers: She might have forgotten the meeting.
questions.explanation: might have done表示对过去事情的推测，意为“可能已经……”。

questions.prompt: Identify the main clause in: 'The book, which was written by a famous author, became a bestseller.'
options: which was written by a famous author
questions.explanation: 主句是The book became a bestseller，which引导的是非限制性关系从句。
